comparison: Both evaluate the core claim that HGT promotes bistability when MGEs affect growth rates (C2, C19, C24-C28, C63). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED through systematic parameter exploration. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, acknowledging it as 'solid theoretical approach' but expressing concerns about parameter space coverage and whether the null model comparison is appropriate (Reviewer 3 notes HGT inherently increases subpopulations, which may naturally lead to more stable states).

Both evaluate claims about death/dilution rate requirements (C29, C30, C72). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these identify critical parameter requirements. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the model's behavior without challenge.

Both evaluate context-dependency claims regarding competition strength and growth rate differences (C32, C68). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes systematic parameter variation. Peer reviewers acknowledge the extensive sensitivity analyses without challenge.

Both evaluate multispecies community claims (C33-C36, C39), though peer result also includes C42-C44. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED through systematic species number variation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging extensive parameter exploration but expressing reservations about generalizability and concerns about the null model (more subpopulations naturally allowing more stable states).

OpenEval evaluates λ value range effects (C42, C43) as SUPPORTED, noting methodologically sound distinction between quantitative and qualitative effects. Peer result groups these with broader multispecies claims (R4) and rates UNCERTAIN due to generalizability concerns, though the specific λ findings are not directly challenged.

OpenEval evaluates niche structure extension (C44) as SUPPORTED, demonstrating findings are not artifacts of fully-connected networks. Peer result groups this with broader multispecies claims (R4) rated UNCERTAIN due to generalizability concerns, though the niche structure finding itself is not specifically challenged.

Both evaluate MGE effects on competition strength (C47, C48). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes opposing effects under different δ values are clearly demonstrated. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'modulation of interspecies competition' as part of comprehensive parameter exploration without challenge.

Both evaluate epistasis scenarios (C52, C53). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate distinction between magnitude and sign epistasis with clear opposing effects. Peer reviewers accept these as part of extended parameter analysis without raising concerns.

Both evaluate antibiotic selection scenarios (C54, C55, C58, C59). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes robustness across different interaction strengths and growth rate ranges. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as part of comprehensive parameter exploration without specific concerns.

Both evaluate metacommunity and regional diversity claims (C60-C62, C65, C66). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate use of Shannon index and clear local/regional distinction. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as logical extensions of the core model without challenge.

Both evaluate the caveat about reduced multistability under certain conditions (C67). Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this appropriately qualifies main findings. Peer reviewers accept this as consistent with specific findings they do not challenge.

Both evaluate methodological validations about genuine equilibria vs oscillatory dynamics (C95, C96). Both find these SUPPORTED as important technical details supporting the stability analysis approach.

OpenEval evaluates reduced global stability interpretation (C64) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct empirical support for resilience testing. Peer result groups C64 with broader implications (C75, C77) and rates SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting broader implications without challenge. Different scopes of evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates connections to natural gut community observations (C74, C75) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without demonstration that HGT is primary mechanism. Peer result groups C75 with other implications (C64, C77) and rates SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the work's relevance to microbiology and ecology without challenging these specific connections.

OpenEval evaluates therapeutic applications (C76-C78, C81) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are predictions without experimental validation. Peer result includes C77 with broader implications (C64, C75) and rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting the work could 'inspire novel treatments,' suggesting acceptance of potential applications despite lack of validation.

OpenEval evaluates modeling framework definitions (C20-C22, C86-C89) as SUPPORTED, noting clear statements and explicit assumptions. Peer reviewers rate the modeling assumptions (C86, C87) as UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 explicitly challenging the assumption that plasmids don't affect each other and expressing concern about biological realism ('same cell counted in different pij runs counter to all intuition').

OpenEval evaluates the relationship between growth rate similarity and multistability (C73) as SUPPORTED, noting this complements main results by identifying another key parameter. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates HGT rate threshold claims (C70, C71) as SUPPORTED, noting effects become significant above 10^-2 hr^-1 with reasonable biological interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific threshold claims.

OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1, C3-C10) as SUPPORTED through literature citations providing appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates knowledge gap identification (C11-C18) as SUPPORTED through citations to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these gap identification claims.

OpenEval evaluates citations to prior work on specific mechanisms (C79, C80, C94) as SUPPORTED, providing biological context for modeling assumptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanism citations.
